key_concepts: Earth's lithosphere is broken into large and small plates that move slowly and constantly.
Lithospheric plates move due to convection currents in Earth's interior.
The lithosphere is made of the crust and upper mantle.
Continental crust is thicker but less dense; oceanic crust is thinner and denser.
Divergent boundaries form where plates move apart and create new seafloor.
Mid-ocean ridges form at divergent oceanic plate boundaries, while continental rift valley
Convergent boundaries form where plates move toward each other.
